title: A typical-start upper bound for low-temperature SK Glauber dynamics
main_claim: For every fixed beta>1, in zero-field Gaussian SK with rate-one heat-bath dynamics, a Gibbs-sampled initial state sigma_0 satisfies T_mix(sigma_0) <= exp(n^{1-1/40000000}) with joint probability -> 1. The corollary adds a lower bound exp(n^{1/10000}) taken from a companion paper.

issues.location: Sec 3, Exact equilibrium inputs (supp mu_beta=[0,q*]); used in Lemma 3 / eq (3) and so everywhere downstream
issues.description: The whole argument depends on the external claim that the Parisi measure has full interval support [0,q*] for every beta>1 (Lopatto2026, v3). This is what makes r(v)=1/beta^2 hold on all of [0,v*], which the entropy-energy identity (3) and the choice rho=1 need. Without it the scalar balance fails. This is a dependency risk, not an internal gap: the paper uses the result correctly, but it is a very strong result (long conjectured) and I did not verify it here.
issues.evidence: 'For the whole range of fixed beta>1, we use the full interval conclusion of Lopatto [Theorem 1.1], specifically version 3. ... Infinite support alone would not supply this input.'

coverage: Re-derived the scalar identities by hand: (2) via Ito for Y*m and Phi plus the pressure algebra, giving -beta^2(1-q*)^2/4; (3) at v* and its derivative for v>v*; p'=-r; r'=4r-6E a^3; the sech^{k+2}/sech^k ratios with the covariance argument; the step-CDF bound on a. Sec 4: law of the GOE orthogonal queries (covariance Pi_{>k}, d_k ~ N(0,2/n)); the exact energy decomposition, including the triangular correction and the H0 W H0 residual; the population identities; the Cholesky and triangular-truncation bounds; the sub-Gaussian and union-bound exponents (n^{1-6l} against the net); the linking density, with |xi|<=2 and the factorization E_B*E_D; the filtration check F in G for the auxiliary reference; Girsanov giving E L = n j(V); the final log-density cancellation through (3), with errors o(n^{1-l/2}). Sec 5: Talagrand T2 for the strongly log-concave conditional disorder, the smoothing KL kernel and the bound KL/delta, the decomposition (9), the Markov exponents, and coverage via two-point contraction. Sec 6: boundary mass, enlargement (12) and its exponents; one-point avoidance, using that the output is conditionally independent of the target G given G(theta); the Hamming step bounds from p(V_b)<=n^{-b/2}; the exponent chain 10b<d/2<2d; the crossing contradiction. Sec 7: pruning termination ((1+a)/2 < 1-eps), the coarea Cheeger bound with constant 2R/B^2, entropy dissipation with constant H/4, the averaging inequality, and the final T and the parameters eps, B, R. Only spot-checked: the Lipschitz induction (13) and the approximation/truncation argument for the transport inequality.
